text:
marco: quick heads-up — metrics team alerted to a small but consistent uptick in cross-tenant cache anomalies after the new prefix-cache rollout. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/cache/hitrate?since=24h . can eng-security confirm whether our current keying could let tenant A warm keys that get served to tenant B?
anya: can you paste the specific metric numbers? is this a hit-rate drop or incorrect data leak?
marco: hit-rate: -6% on short-prefix warmups for v2 path, and ~0.03% of requests returned mismatched tenant ids in the tracing samples (very small but reproducible). not seeing full PII leaks, more like wrong model prompt fragments showing up in logs.
sophia: fwiw the v2 prefix caching intentionally deduped on prefix-only `sha256(prefix)` to maximize sharing and warmup speed across tenants. we did that to improve cold-starts for small customers. it wasn't salted by tenant id.
james: perf profile shows KV lookup is cheap but cache-miss penalties are expensive (extra 12% tail latency on cold requests because of recompile/warm path). sharing increased global hit-rate but introduces the risk Marco mentioned. this could be a privacy vector if prefixes are sensitive.
kevin: quick mitigation options: 1) per-tenant salt in the key, 2) HMAC with tenant-specific key (KMS-backed), 3) isolated cache partitions per tenant. tradeoffs: (1) minimal CPU cost; (2) stronger crypto guarantees but needs KMS calls or cached unwrap; (3) biggest impact on total hit-rate and storage.
kevin: sample key derivation we could use:
```
# pseudo
tenant_key = KMS.get_key(tenant_id)  # cached unwrap in-memory per-worker
cache_key = HMAC-SHA256(tenant_key, f"{model_id}:{prefix}")[:24]
```
this keeps raw prefixes out of shared cache indexes and prevents collision attacks between tenants.
security-bot: audit note — any change that changes keying must be logged for the migration window. we need a record of "lookups that produced entries owned by a different tenant" and outgoing traces pushed to SIEM for 90 days. also: consider rotating tenant keys quarterly.
anya: what's the estimated perf cost of doing an HMAC per lookup? we do millions of lookups/sec on hot workers.
kevin: microbenchmarks: HMAC-SHA256 ~ 0.15-0.3ms per call in our runtime, but we can amortize via per-worker tenant key cache and use a truncated digest. adding 0.2ms is acceptable vs 10-20ms cold miss cost. for hot path we can also do a fast path: if request has `warmup_token` header we bypass HMAC and use shared key (opt-in only).
sophia: important product tradeoff: per-tenant keying will reduce cross-tenant warmup sharing and lower global hit-rate — expect ~3-5% hit-rate loss for small prefix windows. some customers rely on shared warmups to keep costs low. we should propose an opt-in shared-cache feature with legal signoff.
james: rollout plan suggestion:
- canary: 1% of traffic with HMAC keying + full telemetry
- fallback: if mismatches detected, roll back to legacy keying for that canary group and collect samples
- success metrics: no tenant-mismatches in trace samples, tail latency neutral, and hit-rate loss within predicted bounds
we'll run an A/B of per-tenant vs shared for 2 weeks and measure per-tenant unit-cost delta.
marco: agreed. also add an audit-run to enumerate current cache entries that would be affected (hash collisions between tenants) and a script to flag any existing ambiguous keys. can someone own that?
kevin: i'll drop a small script + query in /infra/tools to list prefix digests without tenant metadata and sample owners. will also add an optional flag `allow_shared_cache` to tenant config.
anya: please also include an evaluation of HSM/KMS overhead and a rough cost estimate for key unwrap caching memory. security-bot: raising an internal ticket SEC-2026-045 to track compliance steps and log retention requirement.
sophia: final note — if we go HMAC, let's use domain-separated inputs: `HMAC(tenant_key, b"prefix-v2:" + model_id + b":" + prefix_hash)` to avoid accidental collisions across keying schemes.
marco: thanks — next actions: kevin to open a PR with the HMAC prototype and perf numbers, james to define A/B metrics, sophia to draft opt-in strategy, anya to run cost delta, security-bot will own the audit ticket. will reconvene in #eng-runtime in 48h. :thumbsup:
